Leakage-safe implementation: * no interpolation/backfill of the target; * exact-time lags (1h, 24h, 168h), not row-number lags; * rolling statistics use timestamps strictly before the current timestamp; * recursive test forecasting uses only observed training targets and earlier predictions; * optional chronological holdout validation with recursive forecasting. Expected CSV inputs: train.csv: timestamp, building_id, load_kwh, plus available predictors test.csv: timestamp, building_id, plus available predictors sample_submission.csv: row_id and optionally load_kwh (or another prediction column) The script also attempts to discover files in --data_dir by column names. """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import glob import os import sys import warnings from typing import Dict, List, Tuple import numpy as np import pandas as pd from catboost import CatBoostRegressor TARGET = "load_kwh" TIME = "timestamp" BUILDING = "building_id" LAGS = (1, 24, 168) WINDOWS = (24, 168) ID_COLUMNS = {"row_id", "building_id", "campus_id"} def read_csv(path: str) -> pd.DataFrame: return pd.read_csv(path, low_memory=False) def discover_files(data_dir: str, train_path=None, test_path=None, sample_path=None): files = glob.glob(os.path.join(data_dir, "**", "*.csv"), recursive=True) if train_path and test_path: return train_path, test_path, sample_path if not files: raise FileNotFoundError(f"No CSV files found under {data_dir!r}") frames = {} for p in files: try: head = pd.read_csv(p, nrows=5, low_memory=False) cols = set(head.columns) if TIME in cols and BUILDING in cols and TARGET in cols: frames.setdefault("train", p) elif TIME in cols and BUILDING in cols and TARGET not in cols: frames.setdefault("test", p) if "row_id" in cols and (TARGET in cols or len(cols) <= 3): frames.setdefault("sample", p) except Exception: continue train_path = train_path or frames.get("train") test_path = test_path or frames.get("test") sample_path = sample_path or frames.get("sample") if not train_path or not test_path: raise FileNotFoundError( "Could not identify train/test CSVs. Pass --train, --test, and optionally --sample." ) return train_path, test_path, sample_path def normalize_data(train: pd.DataFrame, test: pd.DataFrame): for name, df in (("train", train), ("test", test)): missing = {TIME, BUILDING} - set(df.columns) if missing: raise ValueError(f"{name} is missing required columns: {sorted(missing)}") df[TIME] = pd.to_datetime(df[TIME], errors="coerce") if df[TIME].isna().any(): raise ValueError(f"{name} contains invalid timestamps.") df[BUILDING] = df[BUILDING].astype("string").fillna("__MISSING__") if name == "train": if TARGET not in df.columns: raise ValueError(f"Training data must contain {TARGET!r}.") df[TARGET] = pd.to_numeric(df[TARGET], errors="coerce") # Consistent categorical treatment for known identifiers. for c in ("campus_id",): if c in df.columns: df[c] = df[c].astype("string").fillna("__MISSING__") if df.duplicated([BUILDING, TIME]).any(): sample = df.loc[df.duplicated([BUILDING, TIME], keep=False), [BUILDING, TIME]].head() raise ValueError( f"{name} has duplicate (building_id, timestamp) records. " f"Resolve duplicates according to the data specification first. Examples:\n{sample}" ) df.sort_values([TIME, BUILDING], inplace=True) df.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True) return train, test def add_calendar_features(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame: d = df.copy() ts = d[TIME] d["hour"] = ts.dt.hour d["dayofweek"] = ts.dt.dayofweek d["day"] = ts.dt.day d["month"] = ts.dt.month d["weekofyear"] = ts.dt.isocalendar().week.astype("int16") d["is_weekend"] = (ts.dt.dayofweek >= 5).astype("int8") d["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * d["hour"] / 24) d["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * d["hour"] / 24) d["dow_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * d["dayofweek"] / 7) d["dow_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * d["dayofweek"] / 7) d["dayofyear_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * ts.dt.dayofyear / 365.25) d["dayofyear_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * ts.dt.dayofyear / 365.25) return d def _history_features_for_frame(frame: pd.DataFrame, history: Dict[str, Dict[pd.Timestamp, float]]) -> pd.DataFrame: """Build historical features from values strictly earlier than each row timestamp.""" d = frame.copy() lag_values = {lag: [] for lag in LAGS} mean_values = {w: [] for w in WINDOWS} std_values = {w: [] for w in WINDOWS} for row in d[[BUILDING, TIME]].itertuples(index=False): b, t = str(row[0]), pd.Timestamp(row[1]) h = history.get(b, {}) for lag in LAGS: lag_values[lag].append(h.get(t - pd.Timedelta(hours=lag), np.nan)) for window in WINDOWS: vals = [v for stamp, v in h.items() if t - pd.Timedelta(hours=window) <= stamp < t and np.isfinite(v)] mean_values[window].append(float(np.mean(vals)) if vals else np.nan) std_values[window].append(float(np.std(vals, ddof=1)) if len(vals) >= 2 else np.nan) for lag, vals in lag_values.items(): d[f"lag_{lag}h"] = vals for w in WINDOWS: d[f"rolling_mean_{w}h"] = mean_values[w] d[f"rolling_std_{w}h"] = std_values[w] return d def s.rolling(f"{w}h", closed="left", min_periods=1) means.append(r.mean().rename("m").reset_index()) stds.append(r.std().rename("s").reset_index()) mean_df = pd.concat(means, ignore_index=True).rename(columns={"m": f"rolling_mean_{w}h"}) std_df = pd.concat(stds, ignore_index=True).rename(columns={"s": f"rolling_std_{w}h"}) # Attach with a stable composite key; timestamps Simpler, safe per-building assignment using original index labels. d[f"rolling_mean_{w}h"] = np.nan d[f"rolling_std_{w}h"] = np.nan for b, idx in d.groupby(BUILDING, sort=False).groups.items(): part = d.loc[idx].sort_values(TIME) s = part.set_index(TIME)[TARGET] d.loc[part.index, f"rolling_mean_{w}h"] = s.rolling( f"{w}h", closed="left", min_periods=1 ).mean().to_numpy() d.loc[part.index, f"rolling_std_{w}h"] = s.rolling( f"{w}h", closed="left", min_periods=2 ).std().to_numpy() return d.sort_index() def get_feature_columns(train_features: pd.DataFrame) -> Tuple[List[str], List[str]]: excluded = {TARGET, TIME, "row_id"} features = [c for c in train_features.columns if c not in excluded] categorical = [c for c in features if ( c in ("building_id", "campus_id") or str(train_features[c].dtype) in ("object", "string", "category") )] return features, categorical def align_features(df: pd.DataFrame, feature_cols: List[str], cat_cols: List[str]) -> pd.DataFrame: x = df.copy() for c in feature_cols: if c not in x.columns: x[c] = np.nan x = x[feature_cols].copy() for c in cat_cols: x[c] = x[c].astype("string").fillna("__MISSING__").astype(str) for c in set(feature_cols) - set(cat_cols): x[c] = pd.to_numeric(x[c], errors="coerce") return x def make_model(iterations=1400, depth=8, learning_rate=0.04, alpha=0.75): return CatBoostRegressor( loss_function=f"Quantile:alpha={alpha}", iterations=iterations, depth=depth, learning_rate=learning_rate, l2_leaf_reg=5, random_seed=42, verbose=200, allow_writing_files=False ) def seed_history(train: pd.DataFrame, cutoff=None): history: Dict[str, Dict[pd.Timestamp, float]] = {} for b, part in train.groupby(BUILDING, sort=False): values = {} for t, y in zip(part[TIME], part[TARGET]): if pd.isna(y) or not np.isfinite(float(y)): continue t = pd.Timestamp(t) if cutoff is None or t < cutoff: values[t] = float(y) history[str(b)] = values return history def recursive_predict(model, test: pd.DataFrame, history, feature_cols, cat_cols): preds = np.empty(len(test), dtype=float) ordered = test.sort_values([TIME, BUILDING]).copy() positions = {idx: pos for pos, idx in enumerate(test.index)} for idx, row in ordered.iterrows(): one = pd.DataFrame([row]) one = add_calendar_features(one) b, t = str(row[BUILDING]), pd.Timestamp(row[TIME]) h = history.get(b, {}) for lag in LAGS: one[f"lag_{lag}h"] = h.get(t - pd.Timedelta(hours=lag), np.nan) for w in WINDOWS: vals = [v for stamp, v in h.items() if t - pd.Timedelta(hours=w) <= stamp < t and np.isfinite(v)] one[f"rolling_mean_{w}h"] = float(np.mean(vals)) if vals else np.nan one[f"rolling_std_{w}h"] = float(np.std(vals, ddof=1)) if len(vals) >= 2 else np.nan x = align_features(one, feature_cols, cat_cols) p = float(model.predict(x)[0]) # Electricity load cannot be negative. p = max(0.0, p) preds[positions[idx]] = p history.setdefault(b, {})[t] = p return preds def weighted_underprediction_metric(y_true, y_pred): """Simple asymmetric absolute error (3x underprediction); use official metric if supplied.""" y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float) y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, dtype=float) err = y_true - y_pred return float(np.mean(np.where(err > 0, 3.0 * err, -err))) def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--data_dir", default=".")
